title: Go and Terraform shared-file feasibility specification
goal: Determine whether a small Go CLI and a custom Terraform provider can preserve Cook's shared-file lifecycle while reusing Terraform composition, saved plans and state.

decision_boundary.proposed_probe: Go CLI -> terraform-exec -> pinned Terraform executable -> generic cook_managed_blocks provider resource -> native repository files
decision_boundary.existing_baseline: Executable Groovy ingredients and recipes; Gradle currently launches Cook. Its current report records 108 passing behavioral checks.
decision_boundary.interpretation: A successful block probe establishes a useful integration boundary. It does not prove parity with the entire Groovy model or authorize a rewrite.
decision_boundary.alternative_after_probe: Retain Groovy with a standalone JVM launcher, or plan a Go core with an embedded HCL authoring layer.

constraints: Use main branch and do not commit.
Keep plan, specification and evidence as JSON and native source files under cookbook; create no Markdown files.
Keep the current Groovy core and ingredient builds available throughout the comparison.
Use only temporary target repositories and local providers; execute no cloud resources or agent sessions.
Go toolchain: 1.26.7. Terraform executable: 1.15.5. Existing local_file baseline provider: hashicorp/local 2.9.1.
Probe dependencies: terraform-exec v0.25.3 and terraform-plugin-framework v1.18.0; record transitive dependencies in go.sum.
Probe provider artifact: registry.terraform.io/the-cook/cook 0.1.0, installed from a local filesystem mirror.
Supported probe build targets: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64; CGO_ENABLED=0.
Ingredient versions remain independent from engine and provider versions.
owns defaults to false; Git is an explicit consumer of exported paths.
Codex and Claude are not classified as ingredients by this probe.

requirements.behavior: Ingredients export values; a recipe explicitly aggregates them into a single file writer. Selecting npm or Yarn without a Git module creates no .gitignore.
requirements.proof: HCL fixtures select npm/Yarn, mount/unmount Git, and assert exact native output and resource counts.

requirements.behavior: A shared file keeps manual bytes outside its named blocks, including CRLF, Unicode, lack of a final newline and manual changes made before a fresh plan.
requirements.proof: Run identical byte-level fixtures through Groovy and the Go reconciler, then through the real provider.

requirements.behavior: Existing blocks require explicit adopt=true. Adoption records original bytes once; subsequent updates preserve that baseline; unmount restores it. A created file is removed only when no manual content remains.
requirements.proof: Adoption, update, unmount, preexisting empty-file and created-file-with-manual-suffix fixtures.

requirements.behavior: Editing or deleting managed content fails explicitly. Any observed target change after a saved plan, including a pending destroy, fails before that target is written.
requirements.proof: Tests distinguish a managed edit before planning from a manual edit after a saved update, creation or removal plan.

requirements.behavior: One Terraform resource writes each destination file. Concurrent resources or independent states claiming the same file must not silently overwrite each other.
requirements.proof: Real CLI tests use duplicate resources, provider aliases and two independent Terraform state directories.

requirements.behavior: Planning leaves the target repository unchanged. Filesystem adapters reject path escapes, reserved control paths, symbolic links and mode changes after preview.
requirements.proof: Compare target byte/mode inventories before and after plan and each rejected apply.

requirements.behavior: npm and Yarn lockfiles are durable input artifacts. The probe preserves package-lock.json and yarn.lock and never adds them to .gitignore.
requirements.proof: Seed both lockfiles, switch manager selection and compare their bytes.

requirements.behavior: The SDK facade applies an explicitly saved Terraform plan, without replanning. A developer can build the provider; a user can run the built probe without Go, Java or Gradle installed.
requirements.proof: Real tfexec integration, rejected stale plans and a runtime PATH containing the three delivered executables and required OS facilities.

requirements.behavior: Measure a two-file apply with the second write failing. Report whether the first file and Terraform state remain changed; do not attribute repository rollback to Terraform.
requirements.proof: Failure injection on the filesystem adapter and a real two-resource apply; decision evidence records the resulting bytes and state.

requirements.behavior: Malformed ownership state, unknown schema versions and malformed block markers fail without modifying files. Removal must not turn a drifted resource into an untracked file silently.
requirements.proof: Provider private-state validation tests and real refresh/removal lifecycle fixtures.

baseline_unsupported.reason: Current public Output.block(String, Closure) has no adopt option; native key/whole-file adoption does not prove block adoption. Record this gap; do not mutate internal declaration maps to manufacture API parity.

out_of_scope: Porting lossless JSON, TOML or YAML reconciliation, whole-file ownership, stations, recipe variants, eject or crash recovery.
Regenerating npm/Yarn lockfiles, installing project tools or enforcing bans on tracked files.
Migrating the seven existing Groovy ingredients or introducing Codex/Claude ingredient classifications.
Publishing registry artifacts, automatic binary installation, cloud resources or production CLI UX.

evidence.observed: 8 actual local_file lifecycle assertions, Terraform 1.15.5 and local provider 2.9.1
Historic Go/single-executable decision; newer conversation authorizes the Groovy exploration. Its 50 ms hook budget is not imposed on this recipe probe.
Public block(String, Closure) lacks region-level adoption options; block adoption is an explicit probe requirement beyond this baseline API.

sources.supports: Supported Go SDK invokes an external Terraform executable.
Module outputs and inputs provide ingredient/recipe composition.
Provider state can store ownership baselines and plan metadata.
Plan modification is the proposed place to capture a file proposal; destroy delivery must be verified.
Failed Terraform apply does not automatically roll back completed resource changes.
Existing local_file baseline uses whole-file replacement.
Groovy can run embedded in a JVM launcher without Gradle at runtime.
Framework forwards PlannedPrivate provider data to DeleteRequest.Private.
